summary: A constructor sets up a new object's fields. Java lets you overload constructors, so one class can be created with different sets of arguments.
notes: Overloaded constructors must differ in the number or types of their parameters.
this(name, 9); calls the two-parameter constructor. It must be the first statement in the constructor.
If you write any constructor, Java no longer gives you the free no-argument one, so Student() is written out here.
pitfall: Putting this(...) after another statement causes the compile error "call to this must be first statement in constructor".
